Synopsis:
Alfira is a young bard who was apprenticed to a woman called Lihala. On their journey to the camp, they were attacked by gnolls, and Lihala died horribly.
Alfira is trying to compose a song in honour of the teacher she loved so dearly, but is struggling. The player can help her play, talk ther through the lyrics, steal her instrument, or even convince her to give up music.
This is a very soft and touching moment in the grove. Should Alfira finish her song (with the aid of the player) she will stand up and sing it in a cinematic scene.

Cluster Contexts:
- DEN_TieflingBard_Bard.json: Alfira is a young bard mourning her teacher Lihala, who was killed in the gnoll attack on the road to the druid grove; she’s trying to compose a memorial song but is stuck, frustrated, and on the verge of tears. This scene takes place in the Emerald Grove amid the camp’s aftermath—other events and NPCs (Halsin, Auntie Ethel, companions like Shadowheart) and celebrations or tense business may be happening nearby. The player is present and can encourage her, help finish the lyrics, grab her lute, or even talk her out of music; if she completes the song with the player’s aid she will stand and perform it in a short cinematic, then put the lute away.
- SCE_Alfira.json: Alfira is leading the kids in a bit of fun moment of constructing their story into a ballad of sorts. When the player arrives they will have just finished up the lyrics and if the player is a bard, Alfira will invite them to play along with. At the end of the duet (gameplay playing animation with music, not a full cinematic) the Bard is given the Shining Dawn ability.
- LOW_Elfsong_Alfira_Lakrisssa.json: Final dialog between Alfira and Lakrissa at the top of Elfsong Tavern.
- LOW_Elfsong_Alfira.json: The end of Alfira's arc. We meet alfira at the top of the elfsong tavern
- SCE_AD_Alfira.json: This AD occurs in the epilogue of Act 2, as Alfira is keeping an eye on the kids. Mol is missing and they're really worried. She muses about she can do to cheer them up/is riding a high after performing with the player in the hopes of cheering the kids up.

context: Alfira is a young bard apprenticed to Lihala, who was killed in the gnoll attack on the road to the Emerald Grove. Now, amid the grove’s camp and its aftermath, she sits with her lute trying—and failing—to finish a quiet memorial song for the teacher she loved, frustrated and near tears. The player can comfort and help her finish the lyrics, play along, steal her instrument, or even urge her to give up music; if helped to complete the song Alfira will stand and perform it in a short cinematic (or invite a bard-player to duet). Though the moment is intimate and tender, other NPCs and events (Halsin, Auntie Ethel, companions like Shadowheart) are present nearby.
